#!/bin/bash
#FLUX -A ZHIHOU
#FLUX -N 8
#FLUX -t 48:00:00

# The following Flux resource requests correspond to the PBS 'select' statement.
# We request 1 task per node, and assign resources to it.
#FLUX --ntasks-per-node=1
#FLUX --gpus-per-node=1
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=6
#FLUX --mem-per-node=24G

# PBS -q was commented out and is not translated.

source activate pyt

#env

# Change to the directory where the job was submitted
# PBS_O_WORKDIR is replaced by FLUX_JOB_WORKDIR
cd "$FLUX_JOB_WORKDIR"


#python run.py --nproc_per_node 1 --master_port 29543 --nnodes 8 ./configs/base.sh &>> basebf1.out

python run.py --nproc_per_node 1 --master_port 29547 --nnodes 8 ./configs/panoptic_2.sh &>> panoptic_bf3_segm.out


#python run.py --nproc_per_node 1 --master_port 29545 --nnodes 8 ./configs/panoptic.sh &>> panoptic_bf3.out

#python run.py --nproc_per_node 1 --master_port 29546 --nnodes 7 ./configs/swin.sh &>> output_bf3_7.out

issues: The job launch command 'python run.py...' is executed directly. For distributed jobs, this will likely only run the command on the lead node, leaving the other 7 allocated nodes idle. It is highly recommended to use the Flux parallel task launcher, e.g., 'flux run -n 8 python run.py ...', to ensure the application runs across all 8 allocated nodes.
